symptom: Login and every write request hung indefinitely; the live feed had been stalled for 7 h 40 min with 14 database sessions queued.
cause: When the PC slept, a database session whose client had gone away kept the row lock on the workspace-state row. Nothing timed out: TCP keepalive was the 2-hour system default, lock waits were unlimited, and the API and worker had no handler for a lost database connection (they either hung or, once detected, crashed and stayed down).
fix: backend/src/database.mjs (+ live-voice.mjs): connections use TCP keepalive (dead peers detected in about a minute), a 45 s lock timeout, and connection-loss events are handled instead of terminating the process. Proven by terminating all 14 application database sessions: API and worker kept the same process ids and served the next request.

symptom: New meetings never appeared: the page showed the 200 oldest of 3,230 meetings.
cause: The list query ordered by start time ascending with LIMIT 200.
fix: backend/src/agent-orchestrator.mjs: return the latest 200 meetings, still in chronological order.

symptom: Totals showed 200 open / 0 completed while the database held 11,359 open and 851 completed.
cause: Statistics were computed from the 200-row page instead of the whole queue.
fix: backend/src/agent-orchestrator.mjs + index.mjs: totals now come from a database aggregate over the full queue.

feature: Live Sync, Overview activity, Data Hub
symptom: The 'recent events' stream was about 9 hours stale and missed new events.
cause: Events are loaded newest-first but the code sliced the tail of the list, i.e. the oldest entries; the in-memory buffer mixed both orders after a restart.
fix: backend/src/index.mjs: keep the in-memory buffer oldest-to-newest and take the newest 50 for the stream.

symptom: Cohort report was always empty (0 acquired, 0 conversions, 0 revenue) despite 2,400 attributed purchases; Planner had no revenue evidence.
cause: Attribution tables enforce row-level security, but the cohort queries ran without the tenant database context and therefore read zero rows.
fix: backend/src/cohort-analytics.mjs: run both queries inside the tenant transaction context.

symptom: A privacy export for a customer with visits, purchases and a lead profile returned none of them; a deletion request would have left that data in place.
cause: Same missing tenant context for the attribution tables, and the customer/visitor selector never matched lead profiles because they are keyed by the customer id.
fix: backend/src/privacy-ops.mjs: export, delete and retention purge run in the tenant context; customer and visitor selectors also match the lead profile id.

symptom: 5,668 ML scoring jobs were dead-lettered with 'artifact metadata not found', and the feed never recovered.
cause: The feed kept scoring against saved model artifacts that no longer existed and never retrained.
fix: scripts/live/generator.mjs and ace_feed.py: a scoring job that fails drops its artifact so the next AI cycle retrains.

symptom: Every signed-in API call took 2.5–4.5 s (GET /auth/me 4.3 s; Boards stayed on "Loading"), against 0.25 s for the unauthenticated health check.
cause: Each request downloaded and re-parsed the entire workspace-state row, which had grown to 23 MB of JSON.
fix: backend/src/store.mjs: the parsed state is reused while the row version is unchanged (a cheap version query per request; writers in any process bump the version). GET /auth/me now 0.5 s, GET /boards 0.26 s; feed median request time 569 ms → 228 ms.

symptom: After a phone call, a lead acquired from Google or Meta showed "call" as its first-touch source.
cause: The call webhook overwrote the stored acquisition source and campaign on the existing lead profile.
fix: backend/src/lead-ops.mjs + index.mjs: call events keep an existing lead's acquisition source and campaign; they only set them for a lead first seen through the call.

cause: The API returned the raw database average.
fix: backend/src/lead-ops.mjs: average score is rounded to one decimal (65.1).

feature: AI Intelligence (page load) and every page that loads several panels
symptom: AI Intelligence stayed on "Loading AI intelligence" for 12 seconds; 20 simultaneous requests took 5.7 s even for the cheapest endpoint.
cause: Each request still made a full private copy of the 23 MB workspace state on the single server thread, so parallel requests queued behind one another.
fix: backend/src/store.mjs: a request now copies only the parts of the state it reads. 20 simultaneous requests: 5.7 s → 14 ms; AI Intelligence loads in 0.8 s; feed median request time 265 ms → 12 ms. Writes stay consistent with the database (verified after each write).

symptom: 0 active routes, 0 qualified evaluations, 0 datasets: trained local models could never become active.
cause: No evaluation policy existed, nothing was ever qualified, approved or deployed, and deployment of local models was blocked by a hard-coded "capability not verified" flag.
fix: The feed now runs the governed lifecycle (point-in-time dataset → train → qualify against a predeclared policy → approve → deploy). The capability flag is now an explicit opt-in, AI_LOCAL_ML_CAPABILITY_VERIFIED, enabled only in this local stack. Result: 6 active routes, 6 qualified evaluations, datasets listed.

symptom: Chronos forecasting was unavailable, and once installed every forecast failed with "Cannot change data-type for array of references".
cause: The optional package and checkpoint were not provisioned; the pipeline also passed timezone-aware timestamps, which the Chronos library cannot process (the code path had never run).
fix: Installed chronos-forecasting with CPU PyTorch, provisioned the pinned amazon/chronos-2 snapshot, and ml-service/src/acemarketing_ml/pipelines.py now normalises timestamps to naive UTC. Forecast job succeeds in about 27 s on CPU.

cause: Optional econml package was not installed.
fix: Installed econml 0.17 with the core ML stack pinned unchanged; the feed submits a confounded remarketing-exposure dataset and the job completes.

symptom: The open queue only grew (12,212 open) and the page, which lists the 200 most overdue, never showed anything new.
cause: Every lead creates follow-ups automatically but the feed completed far fewer than were created.
fix: scripts/live/ace_feed.py: each cycle the feed completes the most overdue tasks, faster while the backlog is large. The backlog is now shrinking.

symptom: Every state-changing request took 1.5–3 s; one tracking event took up to 4.4 s.
cause: PostgreSQL spent about 3 s recompressing the 24 MB workspace-state row with the default pglz compression on each write.
fix: backend/migrations/061_workspace_state_lz4.sql: the column now uses lz4 compression (rewrite 3.0 s → 0.66 s on a copy). Call webhook 1.5 s → 0.6 s; personalization decision 1.8 s → 0.9 s.

symptom: "Run governed analysis" was blocked ("AI task is not active"), and once a job did succeed the answer was never shown on the Analyst tab.
cause: The analyst route only supported OpenAI's API; no code path could produce the qualified evaluation a hosted model needs to become active; and the page tracked the job status but never fetched or rendered its result.
fix: Added an NVIDIA (OpenAI-compatible) analyst provider with access verification and retry on 429/503, a five-case grounding evaluation endpoint, and an answer panel on the Analyst tab. nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b scored 5/5 (cites evidence, recalls figures, declines unanswerable questions) and is deployed; answers appear in about a minute.
